memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the people answered, "Far be it from us to forsake the Lord to serve other gods! It was the Lord our God himself who brought us and our parents up out of Egypt, from that land of slavery, and performed those great signs before our eyes. He protected us on our entire journey and among all the nations through which we traveled. And the Lord drove out before us all the nations, including the Amorites, who lived in the land. We too will serve the Lord, because he is our God." — Josh 24:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The people respond with enthusiasm: "Far be it from us to forsake the Lord!" And their reasons are good ones — they rightly remember how God rescued them from Egypt, protected them on the journey, and gave them the land. Their words are true, and their intentions seem sincere.

Yet, as the next verses will show, Joshua receives their eager reply with a note of caution. He knows that hearts are often quicker to promise than to perform. Bold words spoken in a moment of feeling do not always survive the testing of time.

This is not to doubt the people's sincerity, but to be honest about human weakness. How often do we, too, make warm promises to God in a moment of worship or gratitude, only to find our commitment tested and wavering later? The heart can mean well and still prove weak.

The apostle Peter once declared he would never fall away, and then denied his Lord that very night (Matt 26:33-35). Sincerity is not the same as strength. We need more than good intentions; we need the grace of God to hold us fast.

So bring your commitments to God not with self-confidence but with dependence. Say "I will serve You," yes — but add, "Lord, hold me, for I cannot hold myself." He is faithful, and He will keep those who trust in Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you made promises to God that later proved hard to keep?
2. Why is sincerity alone not enough to sustain faithfulness?
3. How can you depend on God's grace to hold you, rather than your own will?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I do want to serve You, but I know my own weakness. Hold me fast by Your grace, for I cannot keep myself faithful without You. Amen.
